name: Parade of Champions

matches.finish: Serial Killa pins Jonas Weah in 7:39.
Mantua Thunder pins Bomb in 7:11.

matches.stipulation: Television Championship (culmination of an HIWF Gauntlet run)
matches.finish: The Night Stalker pins Vic Valiant in 10:54 to win his first Television Championship.
Champion Alucard Belmont retains over El Diablo Rolande in 14:09.

matches.stipulation: Six-man tag, Legion of Pain vs. Prophets of Rage
matches.finish: The Usurper pins Aero in 17:30 for the Legion of Pain.

matches.stipulation: United States Championship, two out of three falls
matches.finish: Champion Hellfire retains over "Foolkiller" Jason Bell in 24:01.
Wrestling masked under the ring alias "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh, Mr. Shh! pins champion Nighthawk in 12:27 with Legion of Pain interference, then unmasks himself the following night.

notes: The HIWF's own tenth pay-per-view, staged at Texas Stadium. Six of the card's own seven parts are served at this wing's own "parade-of-champions-ppv-1998-06-21-pt1-6.html" (this reading's own delta); the seventh part, carrying the World Heavyweight Championship main event, was already served separately at the page linked above.

matches.finish: The Night Stalker pins Bomb in 0:49, advancing in the Gauntlet toward a Television title shot.
Champion Vic Valiant and Jay Hawke wrestle to a second time-limit draw.
Alucard Belmont pins champion The Usurper in 14:57 to win the title.

name: Monday Mania (22 June 1998)

matches.stipulation: Four-corners match, winner earns a Cruiserweight title shot
matches.finish: The Usurper pins Aero in 24:49 with a rolling reverse cradle, earning a rematch for the Cruiserweight Championship.
Champions The Predators (Nighthawk and Jay Hawke) retain over Hellfire and Serial Killa of the Apocalypse in 9:34.

notes: The World Heavyweight Champion, billed the previous night as a masked "King Pinnacle" Tim S. Hersh, unmasks himself on air mid-interview as the returning HIWF legend Mr. Shh!, dropping interviewer Scott Ryder with a jumping DDT in the process.

date.source: The promotion's own posted date, 1998-08-05 (self-billed "August 5"; posted 1998-08-06).

matches.finish: Champion The Night Stalker is knocked out by Jay Hawke's chair shot; "Foolkiller" Jason Bell then knocks out Tony Sanders and places him atop Stalker for the pin, winning Sanders the title "under questionable means."
Aero pins Bomb in 2:29 after three finishers.
Champion Alucard Belmont retains by disqualification in 14:18 after Aero's ringside interference with a fire extinguisher backfires on Vic Valiant.
matches.note: Jimmy D. Light attacks a returning Vic Valiant after the match.

matches.finish: "The Working Man" Chris Hart pins El Diablo Rolande in 4:35 on his HIWF debut, using a chair.
Aero pins Jay Hawke in 8:48.
Champion Mantua Thunder retains over Vic Valiant in 13:46.

name: Super Bowl of Wrestling II

matches.finish: Champion Alucard Belmont retains over The Usurper in 11:41, amid the champion's own flirtation with joining the Legion of Pain.

matches.stipulation: Winner earns a United States title shot later in the night
matches.finish: James Kira beats Leon Redfield in 13:15 to earn a same-night United States Championship match.
Mantua Thunder pins champion Hellfire in 13:05 after a chair-assisted flying bulldog.
A returning Tony Sanders beats "Foolkiller" Jason Bell in 7:14.
Champion The Night Stalker retains over Jay Hawke in 9:36.
Champion Mantua Thunder retains over James Kira in 12:56.
Ruled a double disqualification in 4:18 after Mantua Thunder attacks both men at ringside; champion Mr. Shh! retains.

notes: Serial Killa also wrestles a mid-card loss to a one-off opponent, Gino Giavante, not otherwise structured here. The card's own "Free for All" pre-show (21 July 1998, collected, not separately served) carries an additional jobber match and recap footage of the previous night's World title change and unmasking.

name: Clash of the Titans II: the Wrestling Classic

appearances.source: Billed on the promotion's own broadcast of 1998-11-17.
Billed on the promotion's own broadcast of 1998-11-17.

matches.finish: James Kira beats The Usurper in 9:34 with a choke slam and the Kira Splash.
Tony Sanders beats James Kira in 2:45 with consecutive power bombs.

matches.stipulation: Television Championship tournament final, for the vacant title
matches.finish: Wrestling masked as "Tyrone the Psychopathic Soldier," Steve Anderson pins Tony Sanders in 3:38 with a Stone Cold Stunner, then unmasks himself and wins the vacant title.
"The Working Man" Chris Hart pins champion The Night Stalker in 8:36, his second World Heavyweight Championship.

notes: A sixteen-man single-elimination tournament for the vacant Television Championship ran alongside the World Heavyweight Championship rematch; only the quarterfinal, semifinal, and final are structured above. The wider bracket (collected, not separately structured): Diamond Rio beat Serial Killa, then Dean Hardt, to reach the semifinals; Jimmy D. Light lost to Dean Hardt; Nighthawk and John Drake wrestled to a time-limit draw, as did Jay Hawke and Mantua Thunder, sending Steve Anderson (as Tyrone the Psychopathic Soldier) and Tony Sanders through on byes; Tony Sanders beat Aero and James Kira beat Mike Oakham in the first round; in the semifinals, Steve Anderson beat Diamond Rio. President J. Adam Hawkins's own written statement opens the broadcast, ordering the World title rematch and stripping The Night Stalker of the Television Championship for holding two titles at once. Chris Hart is also billed, alongside Tony Sanders, as a challenger for the World Tag Team Championship held by The Predators (not otherwise attested in the held record).

name: Friday Fights (20 November 1998)

appearances.source: Billed on the promotion's own broadcast of 1998-11-20.

matches.finish: Champion Steve Anderson attacks Tony Sanders before the bell, then voluntarily leaves the ring; referee Steven Palmer rules Sanders the winner by count-out but the title does not change hands on a count-out finish.

Mantua Thunder wins by disqualification in 2:24 after champion the Jamaican Stud uses foreign-object powder, but a title in the HIWF can only change hands by pinfall or submission, so the Jamaican Stud retains.

notes: Also on this card: Nighthawk, disguised as a woman, ambushes John Drake at ringside and attacks Steve Anderson backstage over a two-week-old grudge (not otherwise structured here); "HIWF December Disaster '98" is announced for 12 December 1998 with Chris Hart defending the World Heavyweight Championship against The Night Stalker, outside the held record.

name: Superstar Challenge (27 April 2001)

matches.finish: Firebug Johnny Pyro pins Patrick Weber after a top-rope DDT he calls the Third Degree Burn.
The Elements win by disqualification after Crusher Zubov shoves Airk Thaughbaer off the top rope and locks in the Russian Ankle Lock, and Luke Kinsey strikes referee Don Davison with a chair.
Crusher Zubov throws flash powder in Synn's face, blinding him, then forces a tap-out with the Russian Ankle Lock as referee Ben Cartwright lies stunned.

matches.stipulation: Intergender tag team match, main event
matches.finish: Lance Heimrickh pins Kano Insano with a German suplex he calls the Heimrickh Maneuver, after an errant Johnny Pyro enzuigiri (thrown at Kano) hits Lance's own tag partner instead of Pyro's intended target.

notes: Also on this card: the owner of the High Impact Wrestling Federation, J. Adam Hawkins, presides over a contract signing for The Stud, who fires and has security remove J and Shaggy (billed "aka Violent J and Shaggy 2 Dope"), his own longtime running mates, from the promotion; the pair beat down Hawkins until The Stud makes the save; Firebug Johnny Pyro then challenges The Stud, recapping their own prior HIWF and SWF history together. This is the reopened HIWF's own first card since the Supreme Wrestling Federation, into which the original HIWF had merged in August 2000 to form the Unified Wrestling Federation, folded on 1 April 2001.

name: Superstar Challenge (25 May 2001)

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.finish: Patrick Weber pins Melvin "Mack" Ebony with a belly-to-belly superplex, after a low blow behind the referee's back.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.finish: Crusher Zubov's flagbearer distracts referee Marcus Miller and strikes Synn with the Russian flag; Zubov pins him.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.finish: Luke Kinsey wins by disqualification after Miss Insano slips Kano Insano a lead pipe and referee Frank Beell catches him using it.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, first round
matches.finish: Dementia pins Johno Insano with an inverted Splash Mountain he calls the Sanitarium.

matches.stipulation: World Heavyweight Championship Tournament, bye-round Fatal Four Way, main event
matches.finish: The Stud pins Lance Heimrickh first, after an errant Johnny Pyro enzuigiri (aimed at El Cholo) hits Heimrickh instead; El Cholo pins The Stud next with a piledriver; Johnny Pyro throws a fireball in El Cholo's face for the final pin, advancing alone.

notes: Twelve men entered the World Heavyweight Title tournament on this card and the one before it; the four winners of first-round matches here advance to face the four bye-round survivors.

name: Clash of the Titans VI: Class Dismissed

date.source: The promotion's own posted date, 2000-05-09, preserved within a later retrospective broadcast.

matches.finish: Champion Mr. Shh! counters a second Time Line attempt with a huracanrana through a table to pin Randall Flagg in 13:30.

notes: Preserved in full within the promotion's own 9 September 2001 retrospective broadcast, as its own "Memory Lane Match." Before the title match, Johnny Pyro and Mr. Friday Night induct Randall Flagg into the Silent Assassins on air. After the match, Pagan, Mark Adams and Dementia beat down Flagg until the Silent Assassins run out and clear the ring. The retrospective broadcast states Mr. Shh! was also the owner of the Supreme Wrestling Federation at the time, and would hold the World Heavyweight Championship for another two months before losing it to Pagan.

name: Superstar Challenge (7 September 2001)

date.source: The promotion's own posted date, 2001-09-07, preserved within a later retrospective broadcast.

matches.finish: Tony Sanders defeats Harley Davidson; the promotion's own broadcast states only the result.
Chris Hart reverses a figure-four leglock into an inside cradle to pin Fatal Fury, who attacks him after the bell and puts him through the broadcast table.
Lenny Getz slides out of Dutch Dixon's End of the Line attempt into a rolling reverse cradle for the pin.
The Insano Boys retain by disqualification after Johnny Pyro throws fire in Kano Insano's face.

notes: Preserved within the promotion's own 9 September 2001 retrospective broadcast. Dutch Dixon strikes referee Ben Cartwright after his loss; President Hawkins fines him $5,000 and, when Dixon refuses to pay or wrestle, suspends him indefinitely and removes him from the Intercontinental Championship tournament, with Harley Davidson named as his replacement. Backstage before the tag title match, El Cholo (Juan Vasquez) attacks Johnny Pyro's valet Fyre, spearing her into a vending machine.
